hook_audit: Beat 1 is a strong curiosity-gap line (a familiar object accused of lying) and it lands in 1.29s, so the words pass the 3-second test; the risk is visual: a static button on cream paper looks like a still image in the first frames. Strengthen it by having a cartoon finger already jabbing the button on frame 0 (no fade-in, no blank frame), with a click SFX and 'LYING' stamped in yellow on the punch, plus a quick red glitch/flicker on the button's triangles to signal 'fake'. Keep the caption on screen from frame 0 so muted viewers get the hook too.

retention_beats.description: At 4.34s the history pivot is the biggest drop-off risk. Do a fast rewind whip: calendar pages flip backwards in ~0.4s (2026 -> 1990) with a tape-rewind SFX, then the 1990 page slams down and the washi tape snaps on.
Animate the yellow timing arc as a countdown that fills while a small '3 SEC' counter ticks 1-2-3 between the open doors, giving the eye something to track through the explanation.
At ~19.5s on the word 'off', punch-zoom 115% into the wire as it visibly yanks out of its socket with a spark cutout and a 2-frame white flash; caption 'OFF' shakes once.
The placebo pill drops in from top, spins 180 degrees to reveal the close-door triangles printed on it, lands with a paper-thud bounce. Keep it under 0.5s so the beat stays snappy.
Cut to dark charcoal; the spotlight flickers on twice like a faulty bulb, and a large yellow 'WHO?' flashes for ~8 frames before the caption appears, opening a loop that carries viewers into beat 11.
Show the brass key sliding into the red keyswitch and turning 90 degrees with a mechanical clunk SFX; the close button on the panel lights up yellow at the exact moment of 'works again'.

loop_check: The line-level loop works: 'remember... This button is lying to you' reads as one sentence. Make it frame-seamless: beat 12 must end on the exact framing of beat 1 (same button size, position, yellow circle), with the cartoon hand's fingertip touching the button on the final frame so beat 1's punch reads as the press. No end card, logo, fade or silence tail (beat 12 has only ~0.08s after speech; keep it), and cut the music bed so its last bar flows back into its first.

cover_frame.title_text: THIS ELEVATOR BUTTON IS OFTEN FAKE
cover_frame.note: Render a dedicated cover still from beat 1 (sky-blue #8FD3FE scene, yellow brass button); keep text centred within y 400-1500 so the 3:4 profile-grid crop never cuts it. 'OFTEN' keeps the claim accurate.

ig_caption:
Why the elevator close door button often does nothing (US elevators)
PLACEBO FILES #01. A 1990 law changed the rules, and one special key still makes it work.

Send this to the friend who spams it every single time.

Sources: 2010 ADA Standards §407.3.4–407.3.6 (door timing); ASME A17.1 fire-service Phase II operation (more in comments)
pinned_comment:
Be honest: are you still going to press it? Yes or no?

Sources: ADA Standards for Accessible Design §407.3 (doors stay fully open 3s minimum; door-close can't shorten it) | ASME A17.1 Phase II firefighters' service. Some elevators do let the button work after the minimum time, so it's 'often', not 'always'.
post_plan: Post Tue-Thu 12:00-13:00 US Eastern (default; test 19:00 ET in weeks 2-3). Instagram caps posts at 5 hashtags, and hashtags help search more than reach, so the first caption line is the SEO question. Trial Reels: a brand-new page may not see the Trial toggle (reports say it may need a public professional account with about 1,000 followers). If it is there, post the main Reel normally and add one Trial variant that changes only the hook or cover; otherwise post normally. First hour: pin the sourced comment within 60s, share to Stories with a yes/no poll, reply to every comment, and send it to 3-5 genuinely interested friends. Cross-post the clean file (no watermark) to YouTube Shorts and TikTok with platform-specific captions.
